claims.claimText: Wisconsin DNR says slow-no-wake speed is required within 100 feet of docks, rafts and piers on lakes; local ordinances may be more restrictive.
claims.authorityName: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
claims.limitationsNote: Statewide summary; posted local ordinances, markers and current conditions control at each landing.

claims.claimText: Wisconsin DNR advises checking signs at public landings for local boating rules, which can be more restrictive than state rules.
claims.authorityName: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
claims.limitationsNote: This does not certify bridge clearance, water depth, channel passability or individual dock access.

claims.claimText: The City of Chetek lists its public boat landing at 726 Lakeview Drive with a $5 daily or $25 annual launch fee.
claims.authorityName: City of Chetek Parks and Recreation
claims.limitationsNote: Verify current fee, ramp condition and access with the city before travel; the City Beach at 228 Lakeview Drive is listed separately.

claims.claimText: Barron County's Veterans Memorial Park landing on Prairie Lake lists a $5 daily or $20 seasonal boat launch permit for the 2026 boating season.
claims.authorityName: Barron County Parks
claims.limitationsNote: 2026 seasonal price only. Do not present it as a 2027 fee without a fresh county check.

claims.claimText: The Wisconsin DNR's 2026 fishing report identifies 11 public boat landings throughout the Chetek Chain.
claims.authorityName: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
claims.limitationsNote: DNR fisheries reporting groups five named lakes; the City of Chetek describes a chain of six lakes. Neither count verifies individual ramp facilities or present operating conditions.

claims.claimText: Wisconsin DNR requires boating safety certification or an accepted equivalent for motorboat operators born on or after January 1, 1989, subject to the DNR's age and supervision rules.
claims.authorityName: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
claims.limitationsNote: See the DNR page for the full exceptions and rental requirements; a simplified age rule is not sufficient.

claims.claimText: Lake Country Marina lists 20-foot pontoons at $200 per day and 24- and 25-foot pontoons at $250 per day, plus gas.
claims.authorityName: Lake Country Marina
claims.limitationsNote: Listed rates are a dated snapshot, not a guarantee of 2027 prices or available boats.

claims.claimText: Lake Country Marina says delivery is subject to availability, handled by its staff for a fee, and requires a minimum four-day rental.
claims.authorityName: Lake Country Marina
claims.limitationsNote: The operator's listed delivery areas and fees should be confirmed before booking; do not promise delivery to a particular private dock.

claims.claimText: Gilligans identifies its tiki bar and restaurant at 2542 8 1/4 Avenue, Chetek, Wisconsin.
claims.authorityName: Gilligans Chetek
claims.limitationsNote: Its lodging page includes a dock slip for lodging guests; that is not proof of drop-in restaurant docking, slip counts or water approach.

claims.claimText: Gilligans says a dock slip is included with its lodging accommodations.
claims.authorityName: Gilligans Chetek
claims.limitationsNote: A lodging guest slip is not an offer of dock access for drop-in restaurant guests.

claims.claimText: Chetek Hydroflites locates its Aqua Theater at 728 Lakeview Drive across from the Chetek airport.
claims.authorityName: Chetek Hydroflites
claims.limitationsNote: The official shows page lists 2026 dates; do not extend that schedule into 2027 without a new source check.

claims.claimText: Red Rocks Amphitheatre directs end-of-event passenger pickup for private vehicles, taxis, and Uber/Lyft to the Jurassic Lot just inside Entrance 2 off Highway 93, recommending the downhill walk via Will Call Trail across from the Trading Post and down Red Rocks Park Road.
claims.authorityName: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre — Getting Here
claims.limitationsNote: Event-night traffic control staff and temporary lot closures control on site; accessible shuttles use separate designated pickup points.

claims.claimText: Red Rocks event parking lots open 2 hours before event door time; limo and shuttle bus drop-off uses the Top Circle Lot (or Upper North Lot at traffic-control discretion), and unoccupied vehicles left past 10 a.m. the following day may be ticketed or towed.
claims.authorityName: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre — Getting Here
claims.limitationsNote: Overnight camping in vehicles is prohibited, and overflow parking may be routed to the Jurassic Lot depending on arrival time.

claims.claimText: Red Rocks prohibits multi-pocket bags inside the amphitheatre; permitted bags include single-pocket or clear bags up to 13" x 15" x 8", small purses or fanny packs 6" x 9" or smaller, emptied hydration packs up to 2L (at most one extra pocket), six-pack soft coolers up to 10" x 7" x 7", and food in 1-gallon clear plastic bags, and items must fit under the 18" x 12" seat space.
claims.authorityName: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre — Permitted & Prohibited Items
claims.limitationsNote: Individual shows may impose stricter camera, beverage-lid, or bag rules at the gates; glass, aluminum cans, umbrellas, and hard coolers are prohibited inside the venue.

claims.claimText: Red Rocks confines tailgating to the rear of your vehicle without blocking adjacent spaces, prohibits glass containers parkwide as well as tents, canopies, amplified sound, portable generators, open-flame fires, and charcoal grills, and allows small propane grills (at least 12" off the ground, flame 6" or under) only when no temporary fire ban is in effect.
claims.authorityName: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre — Official FAQ
claims.limitationsNote: Full-strength beer and wine in non-glass containers are allowed in parking lots subject to Colorado law, while beer kegs, hard liquor, vending, and bringing outside alcohol through the amphitheatre gates are prohibited.

claims.claimText: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre publishes official concert, film, and fitness event dates and door times on its Event Calendar.
claims.authorityName: Red Rocks Park & Amphitheatre — Event Calendar
claims.limitationsNote: Show dates, support acts, and door times can change; confirm ticketed event times on the official calendar or AXS listing before show day.

claims.claimText: Colorado's Passenger Vehicle Traction Law applies on I-70 between Morrison and Dotsero from Sept. 1 through May 31 (and on any state highway when conditions warrant), requiring 3/16" minimum tread depth on winter or all-weather (mountain-snowflake or M+S/M/S) tires, or carrying chains or a CDOT-approved alternative traction device; non-compliance carries a $100 fine plus $33 surcharge, or a $500 fine plus $157 surcharge if a travel lane is blocked.
claims.authorityName: Colorado Department of Transportation — Traction and Chain Laws
claims.limitationsNote: CDOT highly recommends AWD or 4WD in the mountains, and active corridor alerts or closures on COtrip.org control on travel day.

claims.claimText: During severe winter storms as the final safety measure before a highway closure, CDOT implements the Passenger Vehicle Chain Law requiring every passenger vehicle—including AWD and 4WD vehicles—to have chains or an approved alternative traction device installed.
claims.authorityName: Colorado Department of Transportation — Traction and Chain Laws
claims.limitationsNote: Check COtrip.org and overhead highway signs before departure; rental car agreements often restrict tire chain installation.

claims.claimText: Epic Mountain Express lists shared Denver Airport shuttle rates through April 30, 2027 at $59–$129 per guest door-to-door ($49–$119 to transfer centers) for Breckenridge, Keystone, Frisco, Silverthorne, and Copper, and $69–$139 per guest door-to-door ($59–$129 to Vail Transfer Center) for Vail, Beaver Creek, and Avon, plus a $5/seat same-day booking fee.
claims.authorityName: Epic Mountain Express — Shuttle Service Rates
claims.limitationsNote: Dated operator tariff snapshot through April 30, 2027; exact shared-shuttle fares vary by travel date, pickup/drop-off type, baggage rules, and Epic Mountain Rewards discounts.

claims.claimText: CDOT's Bustang network lists West Line, Pegasus (Denver–Avon), and seasonal Snowstang mountain bus routes serving Arapahoe Basin, Breckenridge, Copper Mountain, and Loveland Ski Area from Denver-area transit hubs rather than directly from Denver International Airport.
claims.authorityName: Colorado Department of Transportation — Bustang & Snowstang Routes
claims.limitationsNote: Travelers flying into DEN must connect via RTD commuter rail to Denver Union Station and match seasonal operating calendars and departure times.

claims.claimText: Breck Free Ride operates fare-free local public transit buses across the Town of Breckenridge and Breckenridge Ski Resort.
claims.authorityName: Town of Breckenridge — Breck Free Ride Transit
claims.limitationsNote: Route frequencies and seasonal schedules change between winter peak and shoulder periods; steep private residential roads may still sit outside bus stops.

claims.claimText: The Montana Department of Transportation publishes live road condition reports, highway cameras, incidents, construction, and closure alerts for US-191 through Gallatin Canyon and MT-64 into Big Sky.
claims.authorityName: Montana Department of Transportation — Traveler Information
claims.limitationsNote: Canyon weather and crash closures can change rapidly; verify current MDT alerts right before departure.

claims.claimText: Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport (BZN) publishes official terminal ground transportation, shuttle, rental car, and rideshare pickup guidance.
claims.authorityName: Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport — Ground Transportation
claims.limitationsNote: Airport terminal staging rules do not establish seasonal carrier availability; check individual operator status before travel.
